zoom_image_factor — 2D geometry op

• Data kinds: image → image

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "zoom_image_factor", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: zoom_image_factor (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

Sweeping knob a (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ zoom_image_factor: knob a sweep (docs site)

Sweeping knob b (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ zoom_image_factor: knob b sweep (docs site)

On other images (synthetic scene / photo / coins. Top row: inputs, bottom row: their outputs. Knobs at default):

▸ zoom_image_factor: other inputs (docs site)

*The 4th column is a colour (H,W,3) input. This op handles colour without crossing channels (it does not convolve the colour channel as a third spatial axis).*

Usage

A non-isotropic zoom with independent scale factors for the height and width directions (`0.7+0.6*a, 0.7+0.6*b). Scales via an affine transform relative to the center, keeping the canvas size unchanged (areas that overflow or remain are filled by reflection). Corresponds to HALCON's zoom_image_factor` (Zoom an image by a given factor), and like HALCON, takes two scale factors (ScaleHeight/ScaleWidth).
